einzeiler: Why voters are frustrated with the economy despite strong data ahead of the midterms.
kurzfassung: Ahead of the midterms, new economic data shows a nuanced picture of strong business investment and low unemployment contrasted with persistent inflation and high interest rates. President Trump's policies, including tariffs and conflict with Iran, have driven up the cost of living, leaving voters frustrated. Economists note that while macroeconomic indicators look positive, structural affordability issues continue to strain households.
stichpunkte: Recent economic reports show strong business investment, retail sales, and a low unemployment rate.
Inflation has stalled at around 3.7 percent, driven higher by new tariffs and the conflict with Iran.
Mortgage rates have surged to approximately 7.5 percent, locking many potential buyers out of the housing market.
Wage growth has slowed to 3 percent, causing the real value of workers' paychecks to decline.
Massive corporate and venture spending on artificial intelligence introduces vulnerability if enthusiasm drops.
The federal government now spends one trillion dollars annually just on interest payments for its national debt.
Voters remain focused on high living costs, leading to widespread dissatisfaction that mirrors previous election cycles.

clips.text: Consumer Price Index inflation reached nine percent in 2022, marking the highest level seen in four decades.
Thirty-year fixed mortgage rates jumped to roughly seven and a half percent, abruptly crushing the home-buying plans of many aspiring homeowners.

clips.hook: An unprecedented five-year streak of low unemployment
clips.text: The unemployment rate dropped to 4.2 percent and has remained at or below 4.5 percent for five consecutive years, setting a historic record.

clips.hook: The stark wealth concentration among retiring baby boomers
clips.text: The baby boom generation enters retirement holding massive amounts of accumulated wealth, fully paid-off homes, and high-yielding savings.

clips.hook: A trillion dollars a year just on national debt interest
clips.text: The federal government currently allocates one trillion dollars annually exclusively toward servicing its accumulated debt obligations.

beschreibung:
The economy is one of the most important issues for voters in the midterm elections. President Trump has been trying to persuade Americans that they are wrong to be frustrated about the cost of living.
Ben Casselman, the chief economics correspondent for The New York Times, explains what the latest economic data actually says.
Guest: Ben Casselman, the chief economics correspondent for The New York Times.
